beats.headline: A fleshmancer among the crumbs
beats.text: For the record: Grigori the Placid. Human, level ninety-three Fleshmancer, a hired mercenary of Team Meadow Lark, worshipper of Gula. Elle and Imani hired him and bring him to the Lollipop, where he sits bolt upright between Louis and Linus with a cappuccino, flicking cookie crumbs off his blue robes. Crawler Carl wants him to talk to both halves of Corcunda. Elle reports that he has a stick up his backside. She also reports that he knows what he is doing, and he and Imani have been trading healing tips.

beats.headline: Transferred, and brushing a cat
beats.text: Mercenary ownership of Grigori has been transferred to Crawler Carl's guild. His first duty under new management is brushing Crawler Donut, which she has arranged personally, and he appears to be enjoying himself. Linus, who has been stroking Donut's tail and whispering to her, is taken away by Elle. Grigori's first recorded word comes a moment after, when Donut asks whether she should perform with or without sunglasses. With, he says. She agrees.

beats.headline: He has never done this
beats.text: The plan: take Corky from the Lady Dominators' garage, bring him to Porky, and let Grigori perform the joining. The spell is not difficult, he says, if both halves are willing. They are unzipped, kept alive with spells or potions while pressed together, and then there are a few minutes before the personalities join. Asked what the result is like, he says he has no idea and is looking forward to seeing it. He has never done it. Two halves rarely survive Split Personality for long. The garage attempt fails, and Crawler Carl orders him to spend half an hour learning to drive.

beats.headline: Not built for conveyances
beats.text: Race day. Grigori is strapped into a new seat at the very back of the truck, behind Dong and Porky, stiff and a little green. Hedy reports that the driving lessons did not take. He asks Crawler Carl whether they are going this fast for the whole event. They are coasting to the starting line. His stomach, he says, does not agree with this sort of conveyance. Inside the factory he turns, not to the sink, but to the empty deep fryer, and is loudly sick in it.

beats.headline: He clears the debuffs
beats.text: Crawler Carl orders Grigori into the driver's seat in case they need to move. He cannot; he is dry-heaving into the deep fryer. Then Corky is dragged out of the Dominators' wrecked car into the back of the truck, cooking in his own suit, strung out and unconscious. When Carl calls for the joining, Grigori stands over Corky, wobbling, casts, and both debuffs lift. Corky wakes and asks whether the race is over. The suits must come off quickly, Grigori says, and then asks whether they really have to be moving while they do this.

beats.headline: The joining, upside down
beats.text: The procedure is done standing, once the truck is inverted and running along the ceiling of a room of molten metal. The brains must stay sealed in plastic wrap; spilled guts are acceptable, and Grigori keeps them floating with a spell. He dry-retches mid-instruction and chants. The initial casting is done, he calls; now the parts must fuse, and Dong must hold the halves together whatever happens. Asked about mismatched anatomy, he answers that inconsistencies can be fixed after the race. The brain matters, and both hearts. With ten minutes of the race left, he casts the final part.

beats.headline: An oversight about deities
beats.text: The joining works. Corcunda is whole, and Grull has sent him word at once that he is to be punished; he worshipped Grull before the split. The god comes through a wall. Grigori, on the floor after striking his head and bleeding from the scalp, acknowledges that he should have asked whether the patient worshipped a deity before splitting, and apologises for the oversight. The truck is gliding downward through the air at the time, like a slow paper airplane.

beats.headline: Death as a change of plane
beats.text: After the heat, standing in the back of the truck and failing to clean his robe, Grigori asks whether this is a dream, and whether he is truly still alive. He is. Dong is not. Some believe, Grigori offers, that death is only movement to another plane of existence, and Dong did not think this was the end. Crawler Donut says it is still horrible for those left behind. Indeed, he replies. Told that the court's mercenaries always die, he asks: wait, what? You lived, Donut tells him. That is all that matters.

beats.headline: Examined by the withering spirit
beats.text: Samantha finds him in the garage and accuses the court of hiding him. He greets her as the so-called withering spirit. He is no mere fleshmancer, he corrects her, but the most renowned flesh sculptor this dungeon has ever known. She wants a compatible body and has a candidate. He takes her out of the air, turns her over in his hands, and says he must examine her properly, not in here. She drags him into the safe room. She returns alone to report she doubts his qualifications: he did not gasp at Sam Town, and he is talking to Jamal about his legs.

beats.headline: The AI takes the microphone
beats.text: At the parade, Grigori rides Gonk in the court's procession. Chaco abandons the script and has his wings torn off. The AI wants an NPC on the floor who is not driving and whose voice is strong enough, and settles on the fleshmancer. Grigori leaps off Gonk, somersaults across the ice-cream truck and lands on the back of the subjugated donkey, microphone in hand. From then on he speaks in his own voice, too quickly, with the AI's words. Crawler Carl works out why: the AI could not do this with Chaco, a former crawler. Grigori is dungeon-born.

beats.headline: Eyes that do not react
beats.text: The AI, through Grigori, has already forbidden anyone to heal Chaco. When the court's float passes the donkey, Grigori is standing on her with Chaco at his feet, health still in the red. Crawler Carl meets his eyes, which are the AI's eyes, pulls up a healing scroll, selects Chaco, and heals him without once looking away. Grigori's eyes never leave Carl's. He does not react. Carl then turns and addresses the galaxy.

beats.headline: Released, and confused
beats.text: After the crawlers have gone down, the broadcast shows the AI releasing its hold on the NPC Grigori. He stumbles, confused, back toward the crawlers' garage. In a Syndicate bunker, Prime Minister Victory asks Orren to pull a diagnosis off him. Orren cannot. The AI has locked Orren out, for Orren's own safety, it says, because Orren is being Hunted and only the AI is allowed to kill him.
